validity.recommendation: Correct length to about 100 km and diameter to 1000 only. Keep cost unsourced.
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. It was a joint Polish and Ukrainian project with ENTSOG ten-year plan entries and a page on the Energy Community platform. It is correctly classed as gas transmission. Owners Ukrtransgaz and Gaz-System match the two promoters. Three recorded values do not match sources. Length is 110 km, but the Energy Community page gives 98.8 km for the Ukrainian section and the ENTSOG 2020 plan gives about 100 km in total. Diameter is 700 and 1000 mm, but both sources give 1000 mm for both sections. The 700 mm figure seems to come from a Three Seas catalogue that mixes up the two countries. Cost is 365 million euros with no source; the Ukrainian press quotes about 245 million dollars for the Ukrainian part. The earlier August pass reached the same findings. I did not re-open the ENTSOG PDF today.

fills.researcher_notes: The Energy Community project page titled gas interconnection Poland - Ukraine, read through an Internet Archive capture from April 2024. It is a natural gas project throughout.

verifications.note: main gas pipeline Drozdovychi-Bilche-Volytsia; interconnection between two transmission operators

fills.researcher_notes: The Energy Community project page titled gas interconnection Poland - Ukraine, read through an Internet Archive capture from April 2024. It calls the Ukrainian section a main gas pipeline built by the two national transmission operators, which fits a transmission line. The page does not use the word transmission as a label.

verifications.note: Poland expects interconnector to be in operation by at most October 2022

fills.researcher_notes: A Ukrinform article says Poland expected the link to operate by October 2022 at the latest. The Energy Community page also shows a 2022 end date for the project stages. This is a planned date that was never met.
The 2022 target was missed and the project was dropped, so the delay flag is inferred and has no source of its own. I found no source that states a delay in those words.

verifications.note: 5-8 billion cubic meters yearly, quoted from the Ukrtransgaz chief

fills.researcher_notes: A Ukrainian news article from January 2020 quotes the Ukrtransgaz chief describing a new line with a capacity of 5 to 8 billion cubic meters a year. The recorded 8 is the top of that range. The Energy Community page gives 215 GWh per day at the Ukrainian side, which is roughly 7 bcm a year, so the two sources are close but neither gives a single 8.

No source states 110 km. The Energy Community page gives 98.8 km for the Ukrainian section. The ENTSOG 2020 ten-year plan, read in the earlier pass, gives about 99 km for Ukraine plus about 1.5 km for Poland, near 100 km in total. The recorded 110 looks about 10 percent too high. Not staged as a ref because the sources contradict the value. See the validity note.

I could not find a source for 700 mm on this line. The earlier pass found 1000 mm for both sections in the ENTSOG 2020 ten-year plan and the Energy Community page. A 700 mm figure appears only in a 2021 Three Seas catalogue that seems to mix up the two countries. I did not re-read the 1000 mm figure on the archived page today, so nothing is staged. See the validity note.

The Energy Community project page titled gas interconnection Poland - Ukraine, read through an Internet Archive capture from April 2024. It names the Polish start at Hermanowice and the Ukrainian end at Bilche Volytsya, the storage site.

No source states 365 million euros. The Energy Community page says the project cost is under recalculation. The 24tv article gives about 245 million dollars for the Ukrainian part only. Nothing found supports the recorded figure.

fills.researcher_notes: The Energy Community project page titled gas interconnection Poland - Ukraine, read through an Internet Archive capture from April 2024. It says the final investment decision had not been taken and construction was postponed until it was.

verifications.note: Operator Gazociagow Przesylowych GAZ-SYSTEM S.A; Joint Stock Company Ukrtransgaz

fills.researcher_notes: The Energy Community project page, read through an Internet Archive capture from April 2024, names GAZ-SYSTEM and Ukrtransgaz as the two project promoters. The sheet writes Gaz-System; the ownership team's spelling is used here. The source spells it GAZ-SYSTEM S.A.

The line was never built, so it has no operator. The 2020 ENTSOG plan, read earlier, lists the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine as promoter of the Ukrainian section. I found no source that calls anyone the operator of a built line. Left blank.

verifications.note: Ukrtransgaz chief questions building another line to Poland while existing ones sit unused

status_reviews.researcher_notes: A January 2020 Ukrainian news article quotes the Ukrtransgaz chief questioning the need for a new line to Poland while the existing links are not full. The earlier pass found that the project is missing from the ENTSOG 2022 ten-year plan project list. I found no newer source that revives it. Gaz-System and the Ukrainian operator now work on raising capacity at the existing Hermanowice and Drozdovychi point instead. I did not find a dated GTSOU or Gaz-System statement that formally cancels the new line, so the cancelled status rests on one news source plus its absence from later plans.

summary: Real PL-UA interconnector, cancelled confirmed on thin evidence; spec concern on length 110 vs ~100 km, diameter 700 vs 1000, cost unsourced
